title: OAAP app manifest (oaap-app.yaml), manifest versions 0.1 and 0.2
$comment: This schema is an AUTHORING tool: it rejects unknown fields so a typo is caught where it is made. A node in the field reads more tolerantly (RFC-0012 §8.2) — it accepts a higher minor version and ignores what it does not know, because otherwise every extension of the format would be a flag day for the whole fleet. Strict schema, tolerant runtime. The newest schema always validates every manifest version still readable, which is why this one lists both 0.1 and 0.2.

allOf.$comment: A field added in 0.2 may only be used by a manifest that declares 0.2. The runtime does NOT enforce this — it reads whatever it finds — but an author who uses a new field while still claiming the old version has made a mistake worth catching here.

oaap_manifest.$comment: MAJOR.MINOR. A new MINOR only adds; a new MAJOR is the only thing a node may refuse (RFC-0012 §8.2). Deliberately not the semver 0.x reading, where the minor would carry breaking changes. 0.2 adds app.class.

must_understand.$comment: RFC-0012 §8.2 rule 2: features a reader MUST understand to handle this manifest correctly. A reader missing one refuses this app with a clear message instead of installing something half-understood — the exception that makes 'ignore what you do not know' safe. Only use it where ignoring the feature would produce a broken install; optional additions do not belong here.

class.$comment: Manifest 0.2, RFC-0012 §1.2. What the app IS, as opposed to app.type, which says how it is PACKAGED. 'frontend' (the default when absent) has a user interface; 'service' is used by other software and therefore gets no launchpad tile (oaap.apps.runtime 2.10). It belongs in the manifest and not only in a store list, because a node must be able to answer the question offline, for an app installed straight from Git, and without a foreign list being able to change what its launchpad shows. Deliberately NOT a must_understand feature: a node that ignores it shows one tile too many, which is untidy, not broken.

multiline.description: The value is a LIST. The portal offers one line per entry; on the wire the lines are joined with ';' — so an app parses the single-line form and no entry may itself contain ';'.

endpoints.description: RFC-0016/RFC-0015: at most one non-HTTP endpoint the app may declare; published only after an operator grants it on an 'exposed' node.

wish.description: desired published host port; granted if free, otherwise the platform assigns another (ignored when fixed:true, where container_port IS the port)

fixed.description: RFC-0017 §5.1: the port is a requirement, not a wish. Used by servers that advertise their own port to clients (a media server: ICE candidates carry the exact port). When true the endpoint is published unchanged (host_port == container_port), container_port MUST be in 8200-8299, and a grant fails loudly if the port is taken rather than reassigning.

reason.description: Why this app needs a port past the gateway. Required, because the operator granting it reads this sentence and nothing else — and the schema listed it as required without ever allowing it, so no manifest with an endpoint could validate (found 2026-08-24).
